explanation: Read the smallest unconsumed head from either input until both are exhausted.
correctness: The smallest remaining item must be at one of the two heads. Appending that head preserves the sorted prefix and consumes every occurrence exactly once.
walkthrough: Merge [1,4,4] and [2,4,9] by repeatedly taking the smaller head: 1, then 2, then the three occurrences of 4, then 9. The new output is [1,2,4,4,4,9]; neither input is sorted again or modified.
edgeCases: one input entirely precedes the other.
Empty inputs produce a new empty result; if only one input is empty, copy the other. Equal values are retained with their full multiplicity.
timeComplexity: O(a+b) time: each of the a+b input occurrences is appended exactly once.
spaceComplexity: O(a+b) result storage and O(1) auxiliary space beyond the new result and two source indices.
